tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> moving with an unknown velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi> </mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi></math> undergoes a collinear collision with a body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> moving with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi> </mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>.</mo></math> After the collision, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> move with velocities of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></math> respectively. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> then <math><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> is:

solution.text:
From the conservation of linear momentum,
m1v1+m2v2=m1v3+m2v4
m1v1+0.5 m1 v2=m10.5 v1+0.5 m1 v4
0.5 v1+0.5 v2=0.5 v4
v4=v1+v2
v1=v4-v2
